---
title: "Raw Milk Survey Analysis - 02: Outcome 1, Any Raw Milk Consumption"
output: html_document
---

Model R_Any: predictors of **any** raw milk consumption (`raw_milk_binary`),
among the N = 898 analytic sample.

Run `01_data_cleaning.Rmd` first so `cleaned_survey_data.csv` exists in the
working directory. This file reads that dataset fresh, so edits made in 01 flow
through on the next knit.

Reference categories used throughout:

| Variable | Reference |
|---|---|
| Age group | 18–24 |
| Sex at birth | Female |
| Region | Midwest |
| Cohabitation with high-risk consumer | No at-risk member |
| Perceived taste | Equal |
| Nutrition beliefs | Equal |
| Perceived illness risk | Equal risk |
| H5N1 safety concern | No |
| Trusted information source | Doctors or nurses |
| Education | High school or less |
| Political orientation | Democrat |

```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)   # dplyr, ggplot2, readr, stringr, forcats, tidyr, tibble
library(broom)
library(gt)
library(pROC)
library(ResourceSelection)
library(car)

survey_grouped <- read_csv("cleaned_survey_data.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
```

## 1. Analytic dataset

`data_final` restricts to the analytic sample and folds non-definitive
responses into an "Uncertain/Missing" category for each predictor.

Two things in this block are easy to break:

- `raw_milk_sickness` is renamed BEFORE the `across()` runs. That block treats
  the literal string "They are equal" as non-definitive, which is correct for
  taste and nutrition (already recoded to "Equal" in 01) but would otherwise
  absorb a substantive response category for illness risk.
- Education and political orientation are restored to NA afterwards. Declining
  those questions is missingness, not a substantive category, and leaving them
  as "Uncertain/Missing" makes it the reference level in univariable models.

```{r data-final}
predictors_miss <- c(
  "milk_safety_concern", "raw_milk_sickness", "taste_grouped2",
  "nutrition_grouped2", "household_risk_group", "age_grouped",
  "sex_at_birth", "region", "info_source", "education_grouped",
  "politics_grouped"
)

data_final <- survey_grouped %>%
  filter(!is.na(raw_milk_binary)) %>%
  mutate(raw_milk_sickness = if_else(raw_milk_sickness == "They are equal",
                                     "Equal risk", as.character(raw_milk_sickness))) %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(predictors_miss), ~ {
    val <- as.character(.)
    non_definitive <- is.na(val) |
      val %in% c("I don’t know", "I don't know", "Prefer not to answer",
                 "They are equal", "Missing", "")
    val[non_definitive] <- "Uncertain/Missing"
    relevel(fct_expand(factor(val), "Uncertain/Missing"), ref = "Uncertain/Missing")
  })) %>%
  mutate(across(c(education_grouped, politics_grouped),
                ~ factor(na_if(as.character(.), "Uncertain/Missing"))))

cat("Analytic sample:", nrow(data_final), "\n")
cat("\nIllness risk levels (should include 'Equal risk'):\n")
print(table(data_final$raw_milk_sickness, useNA = "ifany"))
```

`data_interpretable` applies the modelling references: cohabitation is
collapsed to a binary (respondents who declined Q4 join the reference group)
and every factor is releveled. AIC is invariant to the reference category, so
these levels affect printed coefficients only, not which predictors are
selected.

```{r data-interpretable}
data_interpretable <- data_final %>%
  mutate(
    household_risk_group = fct_collapse(factor(household_risk_group),
      "No at-risk member" = c("No at-risk member", "Uncertain/Missing")),
    household_risk_group = fct_relevel(household_risk_group, "No at-risk member"),
    taste_grouped2       = fct_relevel(factor(taste_grouped2),       "Equal"),
    nutrition_grouped2   = fct_relevel(factor(nutrition_grouped2),   "Equal"),
    raw_milk_sickness    = fct_relevel(factor(raw_milk_sickness),    "Equal risk"),
    milk_safety_concern  = fct_relevel(factor(milk_safety_concern),  "No"),
    age_grouped          = fct_relevel(factor(age_grouped),          "18–24"),
    sex_at_birth         = fct_relevel(factor(sex_at_birth),         "Female"),
    region               = fct_relevel(factor(region),               "Midwest"),
    info_source          = fct_relevel(factor(info_source),          "Doctors or nurses"),
    education_grouped    = fct_relevel(factor(education_grouped),    "High school or less"),
    politics_grouped     = fct_relevel(factor(politics_grouped),     "Democrat")
  )

cat("Reference level per predictor:\n")
for (v in predictors_miss) cat(" ", v, "->", levels(data_interpretable[[v]])[1], "\n")
```

## 2. Missingness

```{r missingness}
n_analytic <- nrow(data_final)

missing_summary <- data_final %>%
  summarise(across(all_of(predictors_miss),
                   ~ sum(as.character(.) == "Uncertain/Missing" | is.na(.), na.rm = TRUE))) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "Variable", values_to = "Uncertain_Count") %>%
  mutate(Percent_Uncertain = Uncertain_Count / n_analytic * 100) %>%
  arrange(desc(Uncertain_Count))

write_csv(missing_summary, "Missingness_Analysis_Summary.csv")

missing_summary %>%
  gt() %>%
  tab_header(title = "Uncertain / Non-Response by Predictor",
             subtitle = "Combines NA, 'I don't know', and 'Prefer not to answer'") %>%
  cols_label(Uncertain_Count = "n",
             Percent_Uncertain = paste0("% of analytic sample (N = ", n_analytic, ")")) %>%
  fmt_number(columns = Percent_Uncertain, decimals = 1)
```

## 3. Univariable analysis

Built from `data_interpretable` so categories and references match the
multivariable model exactly. Education and political orientation have smaller
denominators because respondents who declined are excluded.

```{r univariable}
uv_vars <- c(
  age_grouped          = "Age Group",
  sex_at_birth         = "Sex at Birth",
  region               = "Region",
  taste_grouped2       = "Perceived Taste",
  nutrition_grouped2   = "Nutrition Beliefs",
  raw_milk_sickness    = "Perceived Illness Risk (Q7)",
  milk_safety_concern  = "H5N1 Safety Concern (Q8)",
  info_source          = "Trusted Information Source (Q3)",
  household_risk_group = "Cohabitation with High-Risk Consumer",
  education_grouped    = "Education Level",
  politics_grouped     = "Political Orientation"
)

data_uv <- data_interpretable %>%
  mutate(outcome = factor(raw_milk_binary, labels = c("No Raw Milk", "Raw Milk")))

make_uv_table <- function(var) {
  d <- data_uv %>% filter(!is.na(.data[[var]])) %>% droplevels()

  tab  <- table(d[[var]], d$outcome)
  desc <- as.data.frame.matrix(tab)
  desc$total <- rowSums(desc)
  desc <- desc %>%
    mutate(Level   = rownames(desc),
           No_n    = `No Raw Milk`,
           No_pct  = round(100 * `No Raw Milk` / total, 1),
           Yes_n   = `Raw Milk`,
           Yes_pct = round(100 * `Raw Milk` / total, 1)) %>%
    select(Level, No_n, No_pct, Yes_n, Yes_pct)

  m <- glm(as.formula(paste("outcome ~", var)), data = d, family = binomial)

  est <- tidy(m, exponentiate = TRUE, conf.int = TRUE) %>%
    filter(term != "(Intercept)") %>%
    mutate(Level = trimws(gsub(var, "", term))) %>%
    select(Level, OR = estimate, CI_low = conf.low, CI_high = conf.high, p = p.value)

  left_join(desc, est, by = "Level") %>%
    mutate(variable = sprintf("%s (n = %d)", uv_vars[[var]], sum(tab)),
           var_raw  = var,
           Level    = factor(Level, levels = levels(d[[var]]))) %>%
    arrange(Level) %>%
    mutate(Level = as.character(Level))
}

uv_final_data <- bind_rows(lapply(names(uv_vars), make_uv_table)) %>%
  mutate(
    # Complete separation gives uninterpretable estimates; suppress rather than print
    estimable = !is.na(OR) & OR < 1000 & OR > 0.001 & !is.na(CI_low) & !is.na(CI_high),
    OR_CI = case_when(is.na(OR)   ~ "1.00 (Reference)",
                      !estimable  ~ "Not estimable",
                      TRUE ~ sprintf("%.2f (%.2f–%.2f)", OR, CI_low, CI_high)),
    p_fmt = case_when(is.na(p)    ~ "—",
                      !estimable  ~ "—",
                      p < 0.001   ~ "<0.001",
                      TRUE        ~ sprintf("%.3f", p)),
    Sig = !is.na(p) & estimable & p < 0.05
  )

write_csv(uv_final_data, "Bivariate_and_Univariable_Analysis.csv")

uv_final_data %>%
  select(variable, Level, No_n, No_pct, Yes_n, Yes_pct, OR_CI, p_fmt, Sig) %>%
  gt(groupname_col = "variable") %>%
  tab_header(title = "Univariable Logistic Regression: Any Raw Milk Consumption",
             subtitle = paste0("Analytic sample (N = ", nrow(data_uv), ")")) %>%
  cols_label(Level = "Response Category",
             No_n = "n", No_pct = "%", Yes_n = "n", Yes_pct = "%",
             OR_CI = "Odds Ratio (95% CI)", p_fmt = "p-value") %>%
  tab_spanner(label = "No Raw Milk",       columns = c(No_n, No_pct)) %>%
  tab_spanner(label = "Consumes Raw Milk", columns = c(Yes_n, Yes_pct)) %>%
  tab_style(style = cell_text(weight = "bold"),
            locations = cells_body(columns = p_fmt, rows = Sig == TRUE)) %>%
  tab_options(table.font.size = "13px", row_group.background.color = "#F9F9F9",
              data_row.padding = px(4), table.width = pct(100)) %>%
  cols_align(align = "center", columns = c(No_n, No_pct, Yes_n, Yes_pct, p_fmt)) %>%
  cols_hide(Sig) %>%
  tab_source_note(paste(
    "Reference categories listed first within each variable.",
    "Education and political orientation exclude respondents who declined to answer."))
```

```{r uv-screening}
screening <- uv_final_data %>%
  group_by(variable, var_raw) %>%
  summarise(min_p = suppressWarnings(min(p[estimable], na.rm = TRUE)), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(carry_forward = ifelse(min_p < 0.10, "Yes", "No")) %>%
  arrange(min_p)

screening %>%
  mutate(min_p = sprintf("%.4f", min_p)) %>%
  select(variable, min_p, carry_forward) %>%
  gt() %>%
  tab_header(title = "Univariable Screening (p < 0.10)",
             subtitle = "Predictors carried forward to forward stepwise selection") %>%
  cols_label(variable = "Predictor", min_p = "Smallest p",
             carry_forward = "Carried forward")

candidate_pool <- screening$var_raw[screening$carry_forward == "Yes"]
cat("Candidate pool:", paste(candidate_pool, collapse = ", "), "\n")
```

## 4. Forward stepwise selection

Adds the predictor with the lowest AIC at each step, stopping when no addition
improves fit by at least 2 AIC units.

```{r stepwise}
get_aic_candidates <- function(base_formula, predictors, data) {
  base_aic <- AIC(glm(as.formula(base_formula), data = data, family = binomial))
  tab <- lapply(predictors, function(p) {
    m <- glm(as.formula(paste(base_formula, "+", p)), data = data, family = binomial)
    data.frame(Predictor = p, AIC = AIC(m))
  }) %>% bind_rows() %>% arrange(AIC)
  list(base_aic = base_aic, aic_table = tab)
}

selected <- character(0)
step_num <- 1
repeat {
  base_f <- paste("raw_milk_binary ~",
                  if (length(selected) == 0) "1" else paste(selected, collapse = " + "))
  remaining <- setdiff(candidate_pool, selected)
  if (length(remaining) == 0) break

  res <- get_aic_candidates(base_f, remaining, data_interpretable)
  cat("\n=== Step", step_num, "=== base AIC:", round(res$base_aic, 2), "\n")
  print(res$aic_table)

  if (res$base_aic - res$aic_table$AIC[1] < 2) {
    cat("\nNo further improvement >= 2 AIC units. Selection complete.\n")
    break
  }
  selected <- c(selected, res$aic_table$Predictor[1])
  step_num <- step_num + 1
}

cat("\nSelected predictors:", paste(selected, collapse = ", "), "\n")
```

## 5. Final multivariable model

```{r final-model}
final_model_interpretable <- glm(
  as.formula(paste("raw_milk_binary ~", paste(selected, collapse = " + "))),
  data = data_interpretable, family = binomial
)

cat("Complete cases in final model:", length(final_model_interpretable$y),
    "of", nrow(data_interpretable), "\n")

final_table <- tidy(final_model_interpretable, exponentiate = TRUE, conf.int = TRUE) %>%
  filter(term != "(Intercept)") %>%
  mutate(
    term = term %>%
      str_replace("taste_grouped2",       "Taste: ") %>%
      str_replace("nutrition_grouped2",   "Nutrition: ") %>%
      str_replace("age_grouped",          "Age: ") %>%
      str_replace("household_risk_group", "Cohabitation: ") %>%
      str_replace("milk_safety_concern",  "H5N1 Concern: ") %>%
      str_replace("raw_milk_sickness",    "Illness Risk: "),
    p_fmt = ifelse(p.value < 0.001, "<.001", sprintf("%.3f", p.value))
  )

write_csv(final_table, "Table_3_Multivariable_RAny_Final.csv")

final_table %>%
  select(term, estimate, conf.low, conf.high, p_fmt) %>%
  gt() %>%
  tab_header(title = "Table 3: Multivariable Predictors of Any Raw Milk Consumption",
             subtitle = paste0("Adjusted odds ratios (N = ",
                               length(final_model_interpretable$y), ")")) %>%
  fmt_number(columns = c(estimate, conf.low, conf.high), decimals = 2) %>%
  cols_label(term = "Variable & Category", estimate = "aOR",
             conf.low = "95% CI (L)", conf.high = "95% CI (U)", p_fmt = "p-value") %>%
  tab_source_note(paste(
    "References: Age 18–24, Equal taste preference, No at-risk household member,",
    "Equal illness risk, and 'No' H5N1 concern."))
```

## 6. Diagnostics

```{r diagnostics}
roc_obj <- roc(final_model_interpretable$y, fitted(final_model_interpretable), quiet = TRUE)
hl_test <- hoslem.test(final_model_interpretable$y,
                       fitted(final_model_interpretable), g = 10)

cat("AUC:", round(as.numeric(auc(roc_obj)), 4), "\n")
cat("Hosmer-Lemeshow X2:", round(as.numeric(hl_test$statistic), 4),
    " df:", as.numeric(hl_test$parameter),
    " p:", round(hl_test$p.value, 4), "\n\n")

cat("=== Variance inflation factors ===\n")
print(vif(final_model_interpretable))

ggplot(data.frame(fpr = 1 - roc_obj$specificities, tpr = roc_obj$sensitivities),
       aes(x = fpr, y = tpr)) +
  geom_path(color = "#E31A1C", linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1, linetype = "dashed") +
  coord_equal() +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = paste0("Model R_Any ROC (AUC = ", round(as.numeric(auc(roc_obj)), 3), ")"),
       x = "False positive rate (1 - specificity)",
       y = "True positive rate (sensitivity)")
```

## 7. Figure 1: forest plot

Built from `final_model_interpretable`, so it cannot go stale when the model
changes. `clean_level()` handles display labels only; the underlying factor
levels are untouched.

```{r forest-plot, fig.width=13, fig.height=9}
var_labels <- c(
  taste_grouped2       = "Perceived Taste",
  age_grouped          = "Age Group",
  household_risk_group = "Cohabitation with\nHigh-Risk Consumer",
  milk_safety_concern  = "H5N1 Safety Concern",
  raw_milk_sickness    = "Perceived Illness Risk"
)
model_vars <- names(var_labels)

clean_level <- function(x) {
  x <- gsub("Yes, if consuming either raw or pasteurized milk", "Yes, raw or pasteurized", x, fixed = TRUE)
  x <- gsub("Yes, if consuming pasteurized milk", "Yes, pasteurized only", x, fixed = TRUE)
  x <- gsub("Yes, if consuming raw milk",         "Yes, raw only",         x, fixed = TRUE)
  x <- gsub("Uncertain/Missing",  "Uncertain/No Response", x, fixed = TRUE)
  x <- gsub("No at-risk member",  "No",  x, fixed = TRUE)
  x <- gsub("Has at-risk member", "Yes", x, fixed = TRUE)
  x
}

build_forest_data <- function(model, data, labels) {
  vars <- names(labels)

  est_rows <- tidy(model, exponentiate = TRUE, conf.int = TRUE) %>%
    filter(term != "(Intercept)") %>%
    rowwise() %>%
    mutate(var = vars[which(startsWith(term, vars))][1],
           Level = sub(paste0("^", var), "", term)) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    transmute(Variable = unname(labels[var]), Level = clean_level(Level),
              aOR = estimate, Lower = conf.low, Upper = conf.high,
              p_value = p.value, is_ref = FALSE, var)

  ref_rows <- lapply(vars, function(v) {
    data.frame(Variable = unname(labels[v]),
               Level = paste0(clean_level(levels(data[[v]])[1]), " (ref)"),
               aOR = 1, Lower = NA_real_, Upper = NA_real_,
               p_value = NA_real_, is_ref = TRUE, var = v)
  }) %>% bind_rows()

  bind_rows(ref_rows, est_rows) %>%
    mutate(var = factor(var, levels = vars)) %>%
    arrange(var, is_ref == FALSE) %>%
    mutate(Significance = case_when(
             is_ref ~ "Reference",
             !is.na(p_value) & p_value < 0.05 ~ "p < 0.05",
             TRUE ~ "Not Significant"),
           Unique_Row = factor(paste(Variable, Level, sep = " - "),
                               levels = rev(paste(Variable, Level, sep = " - "))))
}

forest_theme <- function(title_size = 14) {
  theme_bw(base_size = 12, base_family = "Times New Roman") +
    theme(
      panel.spacing     = unit(1.0, "lines"),
      strip.placement   = "outside",
      strip.text.y.left = element_text(angle = 0, face = "bold", hjust = 1, size = 11,
                                       family = "Times New Roman", lineheight = 0.9),
      strip.background  = element_blank(),
      axis.text.y  = element_text(size = 10, family = "Times New Roman",
                                  margin = margin(r = 4)),
      axis.text.x  = element_text(size = 10, family = "Times New Roman"),
      axis.title.x = element_text(size = 11, family = "Times New Roman",
                                  margin = margin(t = 8)),
      plot.title    = element_text(size = title_size, hjust = 0.5, margin = margin(b = 4)),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10, hjust = 0.5, color = "gray30",
                                   family = "Times New Roman", margin = margin(b = 12)),
      legend.position = "bottom",
      legend.text  = element_text(size = 11, family = "Times New Roman"),
      legend.title = element_text(size = 11, family = "Times New Roman"),
      plot.margin  = margin(t = 15, r = 50, b = 10, l = 10, unit = "pt"))
}

sig_colors <- c("Reference" = "black", "p < 0.05" = "darkblue",
                "Not Significant" = "gray60")
sig_shapes <- c("Reference" = 18, "p < 0.05" = 16, "Not Significant" = 16)

forest_data <- build_forest_data(final_model_interpretable, data_interpretable, var_labels)

gg <- ggplot(forest_data, aes(x = aOR, y = Unique_Row)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray50", linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_errorbarh(data = filter(forest_data, !is_ref),
                 aes(xmin = Lower, xmax = Upper, color = Significance),
                 height = 0.3, linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(aes(color = Significance, shape = Significance), size = 3.5) +
  scale_x_log10(breaks = c(0.02, 0.05, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2.5, 5, 10, 20),
                labels = c("0.02","0.05","0.1","0.25","0.5","1.0","2.5","5.0","10.0","20.0"),
                expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.1))) +
  scale_y_discrete(labels = setNames(forest_data$Level, forest_data$Unique_Row)) +
  facet_grid(Variable ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y", switch = "y") +
  scale_color_manual(values = sig_colors) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = sig_shapes) +
  labs(x = "Adjusted Odds Ratio (aOR) on Log Scale (95% CI)", y = NULL,
       title = expression(bold("Multivariable Predictors of "*R[Any])),
       color = "Statistical Significance", shape = "Statistical Significance") +
  forest_theme()

ggsave("GroupA_Forest_Plot.png", plot = gg, width = 13, height = 9, dpi = 300)
print(gg)
```

## 8. Interaction testing

All two-way interactions among the selected predictors, tested by likelihood
ratio against the main-effects model, with multiple-comparison corrections.
Exploratory: no interaction is retained in the final model.

```{r interactions}
pairs_list <- combn(selected, 2, simplify = FALSE)
main_formula <- paste("raw_milk_binary ~", paste(selected, collapse = " + "))

lrt_results <- lapply(pairs_list, function(pr) {
  m_int <- glm(as.formula(paste(main_formula, "+", pr[1], "*", pr[2])),
               data = data_interpretable, family = binomial)
  lrt <- anova(final_model_interpretable, m_int, test = "LRT")
  data.frame(Interaction = paste(pr[1], "×", pr[2]),
             df = lrt$Df[2], LRT_p = lrt$`Pr(>Chi)`[2])
}) %>% bind_rows() %>%
  arrange(LRT_p) %>%
  mutate(
    p_bonferroni = p.adjust(LRT_p, method = "bonferroni"),
    p_BH         = p.adjust(LRT_p, method = "BH"),
    Interaction  = Interaction %>%
      gsub("taste_grouped2",       "Taste", .) %>%
      gsub("nutrition_grouped2",   "Nutrition", .) %>%
      gsub("household_risk_group", "Cohabitation", .) %>%
      gsub("age_grouped",          "Age", .) %>%
      gsub("milk_safety_concern",  "H5N1 Concern", .) %>%
      gsub("raw_milk_sickness",    "Illness Risk", .)
  )

write_csv(lrt_results, "Interaction_Multiple_Comparison_Corrections.csv")

lrt_results %>%
  mutate(across(c(LRT_p, p_bonferroni, p_BH), ~ sprintf("%.4f", .x))) %>%
  gt() %>%
  tab_header(title = "Two-Way Interaction Tests with Multiple Comparison Corrections",
             subtitle = "Likelihood ratio tests against the main-effects model") %>%
  cols_label(LRT_p = "Raw p", p_bonferroni = "Bonferroni",
             p_BH = "Benjamini-Hochberg (FDR)") %>%
  tab_source_note(paste(
    "Bonferroni controls the family-wise error rate; Benjamini-Hochberg controls",
    "the false discovery rate. For the smallest p-value in a family the two coincide."))
```

### Supplementary Figure S1: full model with taste × cohabitation interaction

Interaction coefficients are **ratios of odds ratios**, not odds ratios: they
indicate how much the taste effect differs between cohabitation groups.

```{r interaction-full, fig.width=13, fig.height=11}
model_int_full <- glm(
  raw_milk_binary ~ taste_grouped2 * household_risk_group +
                    age_grouped + milk_safety_concern + raw_milk_sickness,
  data = data_interpretable, family = binomial)

tidy(model_int_full, exponentiate = TRUE, conf.int = TRUE) %>%
  filter(term != "(Intercept)") %>%
  mutate(Block = ifelse(grepl(":", term), "Interaction terms (ratios of ORs)", "Main effects"),
         OR_CI = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f–%.2f)", estimate, conf.low, conf.high),
         p_fmt = ifelse(p.value < 0.001, "<0.001", sprintf("%.3f", p.value))) %>%
  select(Block, term, OR_CI, p_fmt) %>%
  gt(groupname_col = "Block") %>%
  tab_header(title = "Full Model Including Taste × Cohabitation Interaction") %>%
  cols_label(term = "Term", OR_CI = "Estimate (95% CI)", p_fmt = "p-value")

data.frame(Model = c("Main effects only", "With interaction"),
           AIC = c(round(AIC(final_model_interpretable), 2), round(AIC(model_int_full), 2)),
           BIC = c(round(BIC(final_model_interpretable), 2), round(BIC(model_int_full), 2))) %>%
  gt() %>%
  tab_header(title = "Model Comparison: With vs. Without Interaction")

int_labels <- c(
  taste_grouped2       = "Perceived Taste",
  age_grouped          = "Age Group",
  household_risk_group = "Cohabitation with\nHigh-Risk Consumer",
  milk_safety_concern  = "H5N1 Safety Concern",
  raw_milk_sickness    = "Perceived Illness Risk"
)

int_vars <- names(int_labels)

main_rows <- tidy(model_int_full, exponentiate = TRUE, conf.int = TRUE) %>%
  filter(term != "(Intercept)", !grepl(":", term)) %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(var = int_vars[which(startsWith(term, int_vars))][1],
         Level = sub(paste0("^", var), "", term)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  transmute(Variable = unname(int_labels[var]), Level = clean_level(Level),
            aOR = estimate, Lower = conf.low, Upper = conf.high,
            p_value = p.value, is_ref = FALSE, var)

ref_rows <- lapply(int_vars, function(v) {
  data.frame(Variable = unname(int_labels[v]),
             Level = paste0(clean_level(levels(data_interpretable[[v]])[1]), " (ref)"),
             aOR = 1, Lower = NA_real_, Upper = NA_real_,
             p_value = NA_real_, is_ref = TRUE, var = v)
}) %>% bind_rows()

main_part <- bind_rows(ref_rows, main_rows) %>%
  mutate(var = factor(var, levels = int_vars)) %>%
  arrange(var, is_ref == FALSE)

int_rows <- tidy(model_int_full, exponentiate = TRUE, conf.int = TRUE) %>%
  filter(grepl(":", term)) %>%
  transmute(Variable = "Interaction\n(Taste × Cohabitation)",
            Level = term %>%
              gsub("taste_grouped2", "", .) %>%
              gsub("household_risk_groupHas at-risk member", "Cohabiting", .) %>%
              gsub("Uncertain/Missing", "Uncertain/No Response", .) %>%
              gsub(":", " × ", .),
            aOR = estimate, Lower = conf.low, Upper = conf.high,
            p_value = p.value, is_ref = FALSE, var = "interaction")

forest_int <- bind_rows(main_part, int_rows) %>%
  mutate(Significance = case_when(
           is_ref ~ "Reference",
           !is.na(p_value) & p_value < 0.05 ~ "p < 0.05",
           TRUE ~ "Not Significant"),
         Unique_Row = factor(paste(Variable, Level, sep = " - "),
                             levels = rev(paste(Variable, Level, sep = " - "))),
         Variable = factor(Variable, levels = unique(Variable)))

gg_int <- ggplot(forest_int, aes(x = aOR, y = Unique_Row)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray50", linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_errorbarh(data = filter(forest_int, !is_ref),
                 aes(xmin = Lower, xmax = Upper, color = Significance),
                 height = 0.3, linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(aes(color = Significance, shape = Significance), size = 3.5) +
  scale_x_log10(breaks = c(0.01, 0.05, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2.5, 5, 10, 25, 50),
                labels = c("0.01","0.05","0.1","0.25","0.5","1.0","2.5","5.0","10.0","25.0","50.0"),
                expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.1))) +
  scale_y_discrete(labels = setNames(forest_int$Level, forest_int$Unique_Row)) +
  facet_grid(Variable ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y", switch = "y") +
  scale_color_manual(values = sig_colors) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = sig_shapes) +
  labs(x = "Adjusted Odds Ratio (aOR) on Log Scale (95% CI)", y = NULL,
       title = "Full Model Including Taste × Cohabitation Interaction",
       subtitle = "Interaction terms are ratios of odds ratios, not odds ratios",
       color = "Statistical Significance", shape = "Statistical Significance") +
  forest_theme()

ggsave("GroupA_Forest_Interaction_Full.png", plot = gg_int, width = 13, height = 11, dpi = 300)
print(gg_int)
```

### Supplementary Figure S2: taste effect stratified by cohabitation

The interpretable form of the interaction.

```{r interaction-stratified, fig.width=11, fig.height=7}
fit_stratum <- function(stratum_label) {
  glm(raw_milk_binary ~ taste_grouped2 + age_grouped +
                        milk_safety_concern + raw_milk_sickness,
      data = filter(data_interpretable, household_risk_group == stratum_label),
      family = binomial) %>%
    tidy(exponentiate = TRUE, conf.int = TRUE) %>%
    filter(grepl("taste_grouped2", term)) %>%
    mutate(Stratum = stratum_label,
           Level = clean_level(gsub("taste_grouped2", "", term)))
}

lvl_order  <- c("Equal (ref)", "Pasteurized better", "Raw better", "Uncertain/No Response")
strat_lvls <- c("Not cohabiting", "Cohabiting with high-risk consumer")

strat_data <- bind_rows(fit_stratum("No at-risk member"),
                        fit_stratum("Has at-risk member")) %>%
  mutate(Stratum = factor(Stratum,
                          levels = c("No at-risk member", "Has at-risk member"),
                          labels = strat_lvls),
         Level = factor(Level, levels = lvl_order)) %>%
  bind_rows(tibble(Stratum = factor(strat_lvls, levels = strat_lvls),
                   Level = factor("Equal (ref)", levels = lvl_order),
                   estimate = 1, conf.low = NA_real_, conf.high = NA_real_,
                   p.value = NA_real_))

strat_data %>%
  filter(!is.na(conf.low)) %>%
  mutate(OR_CI = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f–%.2f)", estimate, conf.low, conf.high),
         p_fmt = ifelse(p.value < 0.001, "<0.001", sprintf("%.3f", p.value))) %>%
  select(Stratum, Level, OR_CI, p_fmt) %>%
  arrange(Level, Stratum) %>%
  gt(groupname_col = "Stratum") %>%
  tab_header(title = "Taste Preference Effect, Stratified by Cohabitation Status",
             subtitle = "Reference: Equal taste preference")

cat("\nCell counts behind the stratified estimates:\n")
print(table(data_interpretable$taste_grouped2, data_interpretable$household_risk_group))

gg_strat <- ggplot(strat_data, aes(x = estimate, y = Level, color = Stratum)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray50", linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_errorbarh(data = filter(strat_data, !is.na(conf.low)),
                 aes(xmin = conf.low, xmax = conf.high),
                 height = 0.25, linewidth = 0.8, position = position_dodge(width = 0.55)) +
  geom_point(aes(shape = is.na(conf.low)), size = 3.5,
             position = position_dodge(width = 0.55)) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = 16, `TRUE` = 18), guide = "none") +
  scale_x_log10(breaks = c(0.005, 0.01, 0.05, 0.1, 0.5, 1.0, 2.5)) +
  scale_y_discrete(limits = rev(lvl_order)) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Not cohabiting" = "#2c7fb8",
                                "Cohabiting with high-risk consumer" = "#d95f02")) +
  labs(title = "Taste Preference Effect by Cohabitation with a High-Risk Raw Milk Consumer",
       subtitle = "Reference: Equal taste preference; adjusted for age, H5N1 concern, and perceived illness risk",
       x = "Adjusted Odds Ratio (log scale, 95% CI)", y = NULL,
       color = "Cohabitation Status") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 12, base_family = "Times New Roman") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",
        plot.title    = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13, hjust = 0.5,
                                     family = "Times New Roman"),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10, hjust = 0.5, color = "gray30",
                                     family = "Times New Roman"),
        axis.text  = element_text(family = "Times New Roman"),
        axis.title = element_text(family = "Times New Roman"),
        legend.text  = element_text(family = "Times New Roman"),
        legend.title = element_text(family = "Times New Roman"),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank())

ggsave("GroupA_Forest_Interaction_Stratified.png", plot = gg_strat,
       width = 11, height = 7, dpi = 300)
print(gg_strat)
```
